title: Exception Intake and Decision Clock Terms, Formulary Benefit
content:
Each formulary of the Formulary Benefit sets terms for exception intake (who may open a request, and whether expedited requests are taken at any hour) and for the decision clock (when it starts, how many hours a decision may take, and how long a request waits for the prescriber's supporting statement).

| Term | Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard request decided within (hours) | 72 | 72 | 72 | 72 | 72 | 72 |
| Expedited request decided within (hours) | 24 | 24 | 24 | 24 | 24 | 24 |
| Decision clock starts at | receipt of the prescriber supporting statement | same | same | same | same | same |
| Wait for the prescriber statement, calendar days after receipt of the request (request date as day zero) | 10 | 10 | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| Member (or authorized representative) may open a request | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Representative other than the prescriber needs an appointment-of-representative form on file | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Expedited requests accepted around the clock, weekends and holidays included | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

## Notes

- A request that a member opens still requires the prescriber's supporting statement.
- On every Northbridge formulary the clock starts when the prescriber supporting statement is received, not when the request is received.

*Hypothetical timing.* Suppose a statement on a standard request is received on a Monday at 10:00. On any of the six formularies the decision is due within 72 hours of that moment, that is by Thursday at 10:00. Had the statement carried an expedited attestation, the decision would be due within 24 hours, by Tuesday at 10:00.
